claims.text: The investigated high-entropy alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with an FCC crystal structure.
Constituent atoms in CoCrFeMnNi exhibit sluggish diffusion at 300–700 K.
Sluggish atomic diffusion delays dynamic recovery during plastic deformation.
Sluggish diffusion reduces dislocation-climb rates.
Sluggish diffusion reduces dislocation cross-slip rates.
Suppressed dynamic recovery causes a high dislocation density to accumulate during deformation.
Suppressed dynamic recovery promotes the accumulation of nanoscale mechanical twins.
Dislocation forests and twin boundaries sustain continuous work hardening.
Accumulated dislocations and twins mediate simultaneous high strength and ductility under dynamic loading.
The proposed initial state is annealed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with 10–20 µm average grain size and low pre-existing dislocation density.
The controlled comparison applies uniaxial compression to 20% true strain at strain rates from 1×10^-4 to 1×10^2 s^-1 at 300 K and 700 K.
Pure Ni (Ni200) with 10–20 µm grains, tested under the same temperature and strain-rate conditions, is the baseline.
At 10% strain, CoCrFeMnNi will have approximately 15±5% higher true stress than Ni200.
CoCrFeMnNi will sustain more than 40% true strain before failure.
At 10% strain, CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit approximately 1×10^15 m^-2 dislocation density, about twice the 5×10^14 m^-2 predicted for Ni.
Deformed CoCrFeMnNi will develop more than 10% twin volume fraction.
The hypothesis is proposed to hold for FCC alloys with 5–30 µm grains over 300–700 K, 0–20% strain, and strain rates of 1×10^-4–1×10^2 s^-1.
The hypothesis may not apply to BCC or HCP high-entropy alloys or to alloys with ultrafine grains below 1 µm.
The quantitative dislocation-density and twin-fraction values depend on composition, thermal history, and testing apparatus.

The hypothesis is falsified if CoCrFeMnNi has dislocation density and twin fraction no greater than Ni at 10% strain, or if its work-hardening rate and ductility are not significantly greater than those of Ni.
